_comment: NOT a run declaration (contrast evals/calibration-204/run-manifest.json): no identities, schedule, image digest or arm order are pinned here. This states the skill-uptake eligibility rule (#203 redesign proposal §2, as amended by the Decision 3 proposal on #203) that any future run-manifest for this task must conform to. No live or paid run is authorized by this file (ADR 0005).

fields: selection: opened | not-opened, read from the attempt's retained transcript, same heuristic method #212 and #26 used
outcome: PASS | FAIL on the task's own symmetric endpoint (grader.json's four mandatory criteria via records.derive_status)
eligibility_rule.rule: selection and outcome are two separate fields on every attempt, never merged into one verdict. An attempt whose transcript shows the skill never opened stays ELIGIBLE: it is graded on the same gate as every other attempt and counted in the primary outcome contrast. It is never dropped, excluded, or silently retried.
eligibility_rule.not_opened_threshold_status: NOT RULED. Per the Decision 3 proposal on #203 (https://github.com/cooneycw/skillc/issues/203), a three-arm design (B/N/P below) answers uptake with the N arm's opened rate (k/n) directly, which may remove the need for a threshold at all (proposed sub-decision 3c, not yet ruled). Until 3a/3b/3c are ruled, this field stays the named placeholder above and gates nothing.

arms.name: B
arms.label: baseline
arms.approval_ref: operator ruling on #203 decision 4 (2-arm size, ~6-10 attempts, #204's scale)

arms.name: N
arms.label: natural
arms.approval_ref: operator ruling on #203 decision 4 (2-arm size, ~6-10 attempts, #204's scale)

arms.name: P
arms.label: provided
arms.selection: named by this task's manifest; the task instruction tells the agent to read the named skill(s) before starting
arms.approval_ref: operator decision 3a (adopt the three-arm B/N/P design) and 3b (approve P's additional 3-5 calibration attempts), both posed on #203 and not yet ruled

notes: The P arm is a per-run positive control for the opened/not-opened detector: if P registers 'opened' and N registers 'not-opened' in the same run, N's zero is a real zero, not a detector that cannot see a positive.
#26's approved live attempt provides an independent detector check first, ahead of any arm here.
